newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rates stable as Paris air cargo enters peak season.
newsitem.headline: Rates stable as Paris air cargo enters peak season.

text.p: The Paris air cargo market enters the peak end-of-year period with the vast majority of cargo rates remaining stable.

"We are in a very paraxodical situation. On certain routes, freighters are leaving full, but contrary to what one might expect, airlines are finding it very difficult getting the market to agree to rates increases," an industry source told Reuters.

Reluctance among forwarders to accept rates increases can perhaps be partly explained by the week-to-week peaks and plateaux in demand which have been a feature of the Paris airfreight market in 1996 and made short-term forecasting a difficult exercise.

"One week we see very strong demand and then the following week it calms down. While overall, there is a net gain in the level of activity, it has become a difficult market to predict," ANA's CDG-based cargo manager, Marc Foussel,said.

Airlines operating on the major export routes to the Far East and North America say volumes have risen steadily in the past fortnight, but, nevertheless, the majority of them have decided on a status quo on rates in the autumn.

This has been largely determined by a relatively mediocre September which saw spot market activity continuing buoyant, even on prime routes such as Japan and Korea and has only slackened since the beginning of October as capacity became tighter.
Korean Airlines (KAL) had hoped to increase ex-Europe rates by between five and ten percent but the plans have been shelved, probably until January 1997.

"The market was just not strong enough last month to give us the impetus to carry increases through. Another important factor was increased capacity from Europe to Korea, either direct or by transhipment, which produced downward pressures on rates," KAL's cargo manager France, Christian Prochasson, told Reuters.
KAL's Paris cargo office had since taken the step to no longer offer spot prices which in effect amounted to an increase of five percent on shipments in certain categories, Prochasson said.

Cathay Pacific is another Far East carrier to rule out autumn rates rises. "While freight volumes have increased these last few weeks it is's perhaps a little premature to talk about a recovery. Given the market's erratic behaviour, it's unlikely we'll contemplate increases before March/April 1997," said Cathay's cargo manager France, Jean-Luc Py.

French flagship carrier, Air France increased its ex-Europe rates by between five and ten percent, from October 1, on routes "where market demand was strong," said Air France Cargo's vice-President Europe, Jean-Luc Servant.

Air France was not prepared to go into detail on rates increases to specific destinations but increased freighter frequencies to Singapore and Latin America - Mexico City, Sao Paulo and Buenos Aires, gave a strong inkling to where these were being applied.

One industry source said the impact of South African Airways reducing its Paris-Johannesburg rates, in order to fall more into line with the market average, had led to further price erosion over the past month.

The trend could be accentuated in the coming weeks when Virgin Atlantic launches off-line cargo capacity from CDG for its three times London- Johannesburg Airbus 340 passenger service. The past month has seen a slight easening in the downward rates on transatlantic routes but the outlook remains mixed.

"With very little prospect of a significant reduction in capacity, we have no real reason to believe why some carriers will desist in "dumping" on rates and our primary task for the foreseesable future continues to be trying to hold rates at their present level," a cargo official for a Paris-based U.S. airline said.
Despite low rates, some "Paris" airfreight bound for the U.S. was escaping to airports outside France, notably the Benelux and the UK, because of more competitive prices on offer.
"One can negotiate spot rates from Paris to New York via London, around 35 percent less the Paris market average," one agent said.

One destination where rates are set to rise is the French West Indies where Aero Cargo International, cargo agent for French airline Corsair, has planned to increase ex-Paris cargo rates to the French West Indies, effective November 1.

"The increases will work out at about five percent and are in anticipation of reduced capacity on the route with Air Liberte likely to withdraw its services at the end of the month," an Aero Cargo official told Reuters.
Air Liberte, which was put under legal administration at the end of September, operates a daily DC10-30 passenger service to the French West Indies.
"Air Liberte has been offering discounts of around 30% on average cargo rates," the official added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
